trajectory_summary: This is a smooth, cooperative call where the rep executed the mechanical structure of the script well — intro, address/roof verification, co-owner question, utility, credit qualifier, and a full bill read-back — without friction or resistance from the customer. However, several value-add moments were left on the table: the bill amount was captured but never flipped into urgency, the interest reason was surface-level and never deepened or used, the sister co-owner disclosure was filed without follow-up on her appointment involvement, and the booking closed softly without a firm handshake or text-follow-up promise.

observed_outcome.quote: Monday, I'll put 3PM. It should work. I'll put it out.
observed_outcome.reasoning: A specific day (Monday the 27th) and time (3PM) were agreed upon for the closer's call; the co-owner (sister) was never explicitly addressed for inclusion, so that field is left null rather than false, since her participation was never resolved either way.

Thank you for kinda clarifying' — the flip into a reason-to-act never happened; the natural place for it was right after the annual figure at 02:44 or right before scheduling at 05:48.

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep asked the interest question early and got a vague answer; rather than probing deeper or circling back to it later when setting the appointment, the rep moved straight into verify checklist items and never referenced the customer's periodic curiosity again.

primary_coaching_focus.why: This is the single largest anchor point on the call — a customer volunteering a $3,500-$4,000 annual spend — and the rep filed it as a data point for the design team instead of using it to build urgency toward the appointment. This is the highest-leverage, most teachable moment on the call.

key_moments.quote: Well, actually, the house is in a partnership with my sister and me, but I'm the general partner, the one who runs everything.
key_moments.stewart_read: The customer discloses a co-owner (his sister) on the title, which the verify section flags as critical for appointment coordination, but the rep only acknowledges his authority ('the boss there') and never asks whether the sister needs to be involved in the design review call.
Customer gives a specific, high annual spend figure unprompted, which is a strong anchor opportunity, but the rep only responds with mild acknowledgment.

key_moments.quote: That makes sense. Yeah. It makes sense. Thank you for kinda clarifying, like, the higher and lower ones too. Makes it easier for us.
key_moments.stewart_read: Rather than using the bill range to build anticipation for what the design could save him, the rep treats it purely as a data point for internal design purposes ('makes it easier for us'), missing the chance to make the number about the customer's win.

key_moments.quote: Well, I don't know. I might have just popped up an ad sometime and replied to it, but, I have looked from time to time about solar for the house.
key_moments.stewart_read: The interest-in-solar question got a vague, low-depth answer, and the rep moved on ('Okay. That makes sense. Let me write that down.') without probing further into what specifically drew his periodic interest.
